title: Global webinar: Key themes for 2027
gist: Promotional registration page for an Oxford Economics webinar (30 Nov / 1 Dec 2026); its only substantive view is that global growth stays resilient into 2027 despite a year of surprises, with the AI boom, persistent inflation and fiscal worries as the key drivers. No data or forecasts are given.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects considerable resilience in global economic growth heading into 2027, despite 2026 having been a year of surprises.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: A major forecaster leans against recession calls for 2027; this supports a constructive baseline for risk assets and cyclicals.
insights.quote: Despite a year of surprises, we see considerable resilience in global growth heading into 2027

insights.claim: Oxford Economics names three key factors that will shape the 2027 global outlook: the AI boom, persistent inflation, and fiscal worries.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: These three are the variables to watch: AI capex as the growth support, sticky inflation as the limit on rate cuts, and fiscal deficits as a risk to bond yields.
insights.quote: key factors shaping the outlook such as the AI boom, persistent inflation, and fiscal worries

themes.theme: Sticky inflation and AI sector dispersion

insights.claim: Oxford Economics frames persistent inflation as an ongoing condition rather than a solved problem; a related webinar title argues that higher-for-longer inflation will dent, but not derail, the Eurozone economy.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Points to a 'slower but not recessionary' Eurozone in which policy rates stay restrictive for longer; this matters for European duration and EUR rate expectations.
insights.quote: Higher-for-longer inflation will dent, but not derail, the Eurozone economy

insights.claim: Oxford Economics treats the AI boom as creating sector-level winners and losers across the global economy, rather than a uniform lift.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: The AI-driven macro tailwind is uneven, so sector selection matters more than broad beta exposure.
insights.quote: AI winners and losers: A global sector view
